Sun, 26 Jul 2026 14:25:36 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.0.2 https://beesayatv.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-09-32x32.png Peak – beesayatv https://beesayatv.com/ 32 32 Pangilatan Peak Loop | Cantao-an, Naga City | 2024 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/pangilatan-peak-loop-cantao-an-naga-city-2024-gpx/ Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:10:10 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=1066 The Pangilatan Peak Loop is a documented 2.56 km loop hike in Cantao-an, Naga City. I followed a combination of community trails and concrete roads leading to Pangilatan Peak before returning to the starting point. The route was short, easy to follow, and passed through areas with regular local activity, making it one of the more accessible mountain hikes in the area.

I completed this hike in April 2024 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedApril 2024
Distance2.56 km (Loop)
Elevation Gain59 m
Duration1 - 2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited

GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started at the foot of Pangilatan Peak, where motorcycle parking was available without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Clear and easy-to-follow trail
✓ Straightforward navigation throughout the route
✓ Frequent communities, farms, and other trail users along the way
✓ Short hiking distance
✓ Multiple turnaround or exit options available

On this trail: peak • sunrise view • sunset view • viewpoint

Route Description

I began by following established community trails that gradually climbed toward Pangilatan Peak. Navigation remained straightforward throughout the hike, with the summit only a short walk from the jump-off. After reaching the peak, I continued around the loop using a combination of trails and concrete roads before returning to the starting point.

The route connected with several other hiking trails around Cantao-an, making Pangilatan Peak a natural junction for longer hikes in the area. During my visit, I encountered local residents along the route and a few hikers near the summit.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Much of the route had limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Stores were available near the surrounding communities, and mobile signal remained strong from start to finish. Approximately 60% of the loop followed trails, while the remaining 40% used concrete roads. I noticed only a few insects during the hike.

Additional Notes

The jump-off was only a short distance from the summit, making Pangilatan Peak one of the easiest mountain viewpoints to reach in Naga City. The peak also has a campsite where hikers occasionally stay overnight. During favorable weather, a sea of clouds can sometimes form below, covering Barangay Guindaruhan.

Kalatkat is a documented 3.5 km out-and-back hike in Kalangyawon, Sayao, Sibonga. I started near Kalangyawon Elementary School and followed a gradual climb through grassy mountain slopes and narrow livestock paths before returning along the same route.

The trail was easy to follow throughout and remained a straightforward walk with little technical difficulty. I completed this hike in May 2026 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedMay 2026
Distance3.5 km (Out and Back)
Elevation Gain184 m
Duration1-2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface30% trail, 70% road
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near Kalangyawon Elementary School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by a mix of paved and concrete roads, and private vehicles could reach the area. There was no public transportation available, although habal-habal services operated nearby. Motorcycles could also continue near the foot of the mountain, but I chose to begin at the school for a longer approach.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Easy-to-follow trail
✓ Communities located along the route
✓ No dangerous cliff exposure
✓ Suitable for first-time solo hikers
✓ Short hiking distance

On this trail: cliff • peak

Route Description

I began by walking through the community before the trail gradually climbed across grassy hillsides. Narrow footpaths used by local livestock led toward the summit, and navigation remained simple from start to finish. After reaching Mt. Kalatkat, I retraced the same route back to the jump-off.

Trail Conditions

The weather stayed sunny throughout my hike. Most of the lower sections were shaded, while the trail became more exposed as I approached the summit. The ground remained dry during my visit, and I did not find any stores along the route. Mobile signal was intermittent, the trail was quiet with very few other people around, and I only noticed a small number of insects.

Additional Notes

The trail was well-trodden because locals regularly used it to move livestock through the area. Starting from Kalangyawon Elementary School added extra walking distance, although motorcycles could reach the foot of the mountain and shorten the hike considerably.
